# Poor Quality Food and Drink

*Page PDF 17*

## **Fare**
Most taverns offer some sort of food to their customers. Tavern meals tend to be hearty but simple and sold at slightly inflated prices. Gold Tier venues make more of an effort and may be compared to restaurants in terms of their quality. Unscrupulous landlords are not concerned about using stale ingredients and unhygienic cooking practices. 

## **None**
There is no food at the venue. 

## **Snacks**
Snacks may stave off hunger but are hardly nourishing. A visitor to a tavern who tries to live off snacks could do so for a number of days equal to their Toughness Bonus but have to test for Starvation if they persist beyond this time without proper food. 

_**Examples:** Dried Hagercryb Shaggy Strips, Fried Vorbergland Hog Rinds, Trinkwort Crisps, StrigoiToast_ **Fair Price:** 2d 

## **Fine Menu**
Prepared by a trained cook, a fine menu consists of fine quality meals at double the normal price. Not only will the food be expertly prepared, but it will be served with side dishes and a sweet dessert. Fine quality snacks and stews will also be available. 

_**Examples:** Razorbeak Eggs and Spinach, Roast Daggerfish with Seabeet, Silverside of Stimmigen Dairy baked with Tarrabeth and served with Turnip Mash, Terrine of Stirpike with Peas and Artichokes, Fillet of Averland Shorthorn with Honey-Glazed Roast Parsnips, Sauerapfel Pie with Cream_ 

## **Lavish Menu**
A lavish menu consists of dishes prepared from the finest ingredients and cooked by some of the best chefs in the Empire. This food is excellent but costs three times the usual price. Fine quality snacks and stews will also be available, though the proprietors may expect them to be consumed as part of a meal and may regard a guest who lives on such food as tight-fisted and déclassé. 

## **Stew**
Stews and soups are often served at taverns together with hunks of stale bread. They are easy to make and nutritious enough that a Character may subsist on stew and never have to worry about Starvation. 

_**Examples:** Fleeceback Stew, Goulash in the Sylvanian Style, Reconstituted Stockfish_ **Fair Price:** 4d 

## **Simple Meal**
Simple meals tend to be made from locally sourced food, cheap vegetables, and less desirable cuts of meat. 

_**Examples:** Vorbergland Hog chops with Sauerkraut and a slice of Bread, chunks of boiled Fleeceback with mashed Turnips, stewed tail of Stolz Fathead with Root Vegetables_ **Fair Price:** 10d 

## **Meal**
A square meal in the empire consists of a mixture of grains, vegetables, and meat or fish, accompanied by slices of fresh bread. 

_**Examples:** Lurkerfish and Gymmcrab Soup, Slice of Reik Eel Pie, Fathead Tripes with Sauerkraut, Kuri (spiced goat meat prepared according to a Dwarf recipe)_ **Fair Price:** 1/- 

_**Examples:** A single meal may involve Tilean Olives stuffed with Sprinthof Smoked Cheese as an Amuse Bouche, Gymmcrab Bisque to start, Ribeye of Stolz Fathead with Roast Vegetables as a main meal, and a choice selection of Friedendorf Sweetmeats_ 

## Poor Quality Food and Drink
Poor meals tend to be the same sort of food as regular meals but may be noticeably stale, made with fewer ingredients, or served undercooked or burned. Bacteria and mould can propagate in such food and make people ill. Poor quality drinks do not tend to harbour infection due to their alcoholic content but may still cause illness due to poisonous chemicals or a nauseating taste. 

A Character may notice that food or drink is of poor quality if they pass an **Easy (+40) Perception (Smell), Perception (Taste), Trade (Brewer),** or **Trade (Cook)** Test. Poor meals cost half the price of a regular meal, but anyone consuming them runs a risk of illness. 

The GM should make a Secret Test, rolling a 1d10 for each Character who consumes poor quality food or drink. On a roll of 1, that Character risks becoming ill and must test for contraction of the Galloping Trots (see **WFRP** , page 187). 

## **Menu**
A menu consists of a variety of food, enabling patrons to buy either stews, simple meals, or meals at normal prices.
